messages:
Sam: FYI saw two gpu nodes in eu-west-2 get scaled down by the autoscaler around 03:12 UTC and a couple of long-running training jobs failed to reschedule. Seems PDBs blocked eviction for the stateful sidecars so drain never completed and CA forced the node gone anyway.
Priya: wait, CA shouldn't delete a node with non-evictable pods. Do you have the CA logs? @miguel can you check cluster-autoscaler events?
Miguel: I pulled the logs quickly — CA triggered scale-down because node was under 20% util and "ScaleDownUnneededTime" expired. It tried to evict pods but hit PodDisruptionBudget violations for 2 pods (metrics-exporter + checkpoint-sync). After 5m the node became NotReady and kubelet reported NotReady -> node was removed by cloud provider, leaving pods orphaned.
Jordan: ugh. So the sequence was: CA starts drain -> evictions blocked by PDB -> kubelet flapped -> cloud provider reclaimed instance -> pods stuck in Terminating or recreated on other nodes but couldn't get GPUs assigned? Any GPU scheduling errors?
Sam: Yes. The training pods were Pending with events: "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" because remaining nodes were already full. Checkpoint-sync got stuck in Terminating so the job lost state.
Priya: Two things to tackle: immediate mitigation to avoid more job losses tonight, and long-term policy changes.
Miguel: Immediate fix: increase ScaleDownDelay or disable scale-down for gpu-pool-eu-west-2 until we fix PDBs. Quick command: `kubectl annotate nodepool/gpu-pool-eu-west-2 cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true` (our infra supports that)
Jordan: Also we should add a short-lived admission webhook to reject PDBs that would block all replicas on a single nodepool. But that's longer-term.
Sam: For tonight I applied the annotation and bumped ScaleDownUnneededTime to 20m for that pool. Also cordoned the two remaining gpu nodes we don't want to lose.
devops-bot: cluster-autoscaler: scale-down disabled for nodepool/gpu-pool-eu-west-2 by Sam at 1792005478
Priya: For policy: let's audit all PDBs with `kubectl get pdb --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name}:{.spec}{"\n"}{end}'` and flag ones with `minAvailable` equal to replica count (i.e., 100% protected). PDBs that lock all replicas on the same nodepool are dangerous.
Miguel: Agree. Also consider switching some PDBs to `maxUnavailable: 1` instead of `minAvailable: X` for non-critical infra. maxUnavailable is more scale-down-friendly.
Jordan: Question: can we use PriorityClass to allow CA to evict lower-priority pods first? Does that help with PDBs?
Priya: PriorityClass only affects preemption and scheduling, it doesn't directly bypass PDBs. Eviction is still blocked by PDB constraints. But we can use priority classes to classify critical vs batch; then for critical pods we create resilient PDBs or replica placements across zones.
Sam: Another pattern: put stateful sidecars (checkpoint-sync/metrics) on a separate nodepool with no aggressive scale-down, or run them as DaemonSets where appropriate. That way evictions won't be blocked by a PDB that couples a sidecar + GPU pod.
Miguel: We found two concrete misconfigs: 1) PDB for checkpoint-sync had minAvailable: 1 while the deployment had only 1 replica pinned to the same node by anti-affinity missing. 2) metrics-exporter had PDB preventing any disruption but is non-critical — should be maxUnavailable: 100%.
Jordan: Action items then?
Priya: I'll create a PR to: (a) audit PDBs and convert non-critical minAvailable->maxUnavailable, (b) add nodepool annotation to infra docs to opt-out of scale-down for stateful pools, (c) create a k8s policy to detect PDBs that could block scale-down.
Sam: I'll keep scale-down disabled on the pool and move today's training jobs to a burst pool (spot-gpu) to free capacity.
Miguel: I'll add a cluster-autoscaler alert when a nodepool has >1 failed drains in 15m. CA already exposes events; we'll alert on `FailedDrain` count.
Jordan: Long term: consider implementing a small controller that checks PDB coverage vs topology spread (nodepool/zone) and warns when PDB + topology would pin all replicas to a single pool.
Priya: Also let's update runbooks: - When CA evicts a gpu node and pods stuck: cordon new nodes, disable scale-down for pool, check PDBs, review node conditions (NetworkUnavailable?), then drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120` only after ensuring checkpoint persisted.
Sam: Note on cost: leaving pool unsubdued overnight costs ~0.5k USD/day for that pool. We need the audit completed in 24h so we can re-enable scale-down before Monday. I'll track cost impact in #finance later.
Miguel: Small config snippet to detect risky PDBs (pseudo):
```sh
kubectl get pdb -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.minAvailable == .metadata.annotations.replicas) | {ns:.metadata.namespace,name:.metadata.name}'
```
(not perfect but quick)
Jordan: Thanks. Can someone file a short postmortem once PRs merged? We avoided data loss for most jobs but had one job restart and lose progress.
Sam: On it. Will post summary tomorrow.
Priya: 👍 I'll start the PDB PR and ping infra for the nodepool annotation change.
Miguel: I'll own the CA alert and the quick jq audit script in ops repo.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: created issue #457 (pdb-audit-and-scale-down-hardening) referenced by Sam, Priya, Miguel at 1792005508 :white_check_mark:
Sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
